title: allow setting another devfs ruleset
body:
Hi,

Thanks for the amazing tool podman.
I'm using it on FreeBSD and after an hour of debugging the devfs mount ruleset I found that the ruleset was hardcoded to 4.
That happens on this line:
https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/eeeb322d33186b6fdb8522de61ac442c0ae7de81/pkg/specgen/generate/oci_freebsd.go#L95

Would it be an idea to make the ruleset a variable that the operator can set? With a default of 4.

comments.body:
Hi, I'd like to work on this. If I read oci_freebsd.go correctly, the ruleset is only used
for the Linux-emulation devfs mount, next to the hardcoded "rule=path shm unhide".
I'd keep 4 as the default. Which would you prefer for setting it: a containers.conf option
(needs a change in containers/common), an annotation, or a podman run flag?
I can't run FreeBSD locally, so I'd add a unit test for the option building and
cross-compile for GOOS=freebsd. Would that be acceptable?

please follow our issue template, i.e. feature request, in the future.

I cant speak to freebsd at all, that is maintained by @dfr

If you need to expose a device or devices to a container, you can use Podman's `--device` option. This uses the hard-coded ruleset 4 as a base and modifies the container's devfs instance to expose the selected device nodes. For FreeBSD-native containers, the ruleset choice happens in the runtime-tools package [here](https://github.com/opencontainers/runtime-tools/blob/master/generate/generate.go#L251).

I'm not opposed to making the ruleset variable but first, I would like to understand why `--device`  is not enough for your use-case.

I tried --device /dev/bpf to enable the use of a dhcp client. Maybe I don't understand it correctly, but I also seem to need --device /dev/bpf0, but this is a symlink which was not exposed to the jail afterwards.
So I couldn't get it to work with --device.
After adding `add path 'bpf*' unhide` to "devfsrules_jail=4" it worked. But I don't like changing global defaults for only a specific container. That is how I came to asking for having devfs_ruleset as an option.

I'm also open for other solutions to my bpf problem.

Thanks for the clarification - it might be possible to fix `--device` to accept the wildcard. In the meantime you could try `--privileged` which mounts the full devfs into the container, just for experimentation.

EDIT: I did some testing with `ocijail` and if we can get Podman to accept `/dev/bpf*` as a valid device name and pass it down to `ocijail`, then it does unhide both `bpf` and the `bpf0` symlink.
